doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop and the first American trip
title: When he visited and how he learned bebop
summary: He places the trip in winter, and says he learned bebop vocabulary from records and on the spot.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What month were you there? So it was 1947 and you’re in New York. You’re at the Three Deuces. Do you remember at least the season? Was it spring, summer, fall, winter?
It must, must have been… because… excuse me… the festival in Nice, where I had to join the Belgian delegation… [laughs] And that was… it must have been something like February or something.
So in the winter, you were in New York.
Not autumn in New York. You’re winter in New York.
Maybe. But I didn’t… there was no snow that I remember.
Okay, okay. So you have expansive harmonic knowledge by the time you’re playing bebop.
Is this all self-taught, or did you have somebody help you, or was this like musicians…?

No, the… Well, I learned on the spot, you know, and whenever I’d see another [good reader?]. And the records were enough for me. If you can play all the bebop runs, you know, and apply them. Not just play, be a clone. That’s what I always try to, even now, especially now.
